title: Per-key durable ShipStation limiter and AbortSignal threading

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every ShipStation v2 request enters one per-API-key admission owner, and two process-local limiter instances consume one shared durable budget while different keys remain isolated.
Provider Retry-After pauses the shared key across processes, and one caller signal covers admission, fetch, Retry-After, 5xx backoff, and outer retry attempts without overlapping timed-out work.

Admission order is interactive before batch before background; recalculation/backfill uses batch, sync and recovery reads use background, and label create, void, and return operations remain interactive.
Cross-order, cross-account, and mismatched selected-rate facts still fail before provider activity, so limiter and cancellation plumbing does not weaken the backend rate or label boundary.
Strict TypeScript, production frontend build, ticket-specific guards, mandatory exact-rate and provider-timeout checks, and all 49 source-of-truth guards pass at the reviewed implementation SHA.

The exact implementation SHA is live on Vercel and the Render API, sync worker, and print worker with RATE_LIMITER_BACKEND=durable on every ShipStation-calling process; verification was read-only and caused no label, postage, marketplace, or production data side effect.

canonicalOwners: src/lib/shipstation/client.ts owns ShipStation v2 admission, priority, request-wide cancellation, retries, and shared Retry-After deferral
src/lib/shipstation/durable-rate-limiter.ts owns atomic Postgres-backed per-key token state and fleet-wide pause state
src/services/rates.ts owns only local quote-fanout concurrency ordering and delegates provider admission to the ShipStation client
src/services/with-timeout-retry.ts owns attempt-scoped cancellation and waits for a timed-out attempt to settle before retry

oldOwners.path: process-local ShipStation v2 token buckets and request-local Retry-After sleep
outer timeout wrappers that could reject without aborting or settling the active attempt

oldOwners.delegatesTo: src/services/rates.ts strict interactive, batch, then background queue

wrappers.delegatesTo: the caller AbortSignal composed with the helper's local timeout signal
src/lib/shipstation/client.ts for priority-aware, cancellable provider requests

sotBypass.details: No frontend or connector mints rate truth, chooses a best rate, or bypasses label authorization. Provider admission and cancellation are centralized below the existing backend rate and label owners.

evidence.proves: Two limiter instances sharing one injected store model separate processes: the same key consumes one combined budget, another key is isolated, a shared pause reaches the second instance, caller abort reaches fetch, and priority wiring remains strict.

Cancellation stops permit polling, a shared provider pause cannot be bypassed by another process, the caller signal is not replaced by a local timeout, and label mutations are never demoted to batch or background.

RATE_LIMITER_BACKEND was read back as durable on API, sync, and print services; startup logs showed API listening, sync scheduler/rate-browse worker started, and print-queue worker started. Readiness returned HTTP 200. Deep health remained degraded only for one partial order-status catch-up pass while shipment sync was actively running; db, dbWrite, orders, printQueue, printQueueWorker, fulfillmentOutbox, and eventLoop were green.

The reviewed implementation contains the canonical admission, durable state, signal propagation, priority routing, focused tests, and ticket documentation. It adds no migration and does not alter shipped/cancelled protections, purchase a label, charge postage, notify a marketplace, or mutate production data.

migrations.rollbackPlan: No schema or data rollback is required. Set RATE_LIMITER_BACKEND=memory on API, sync worker, and print worker for an immediate operational rollback, then deploy a reviewed forward-revert of 956cf41f8eba1c69ea634c9e8ba2eb70c5485253 if code rollback is required.

rollback.strategy: First switch RATE_LIMITER_BACKEND to memory on all three ShipStation-calling Render services if durable admission causes an incident. If code rollback is still required, forward-revert the packet-only commit and implementation SHA, then redeploy the same reviewed rollback SHA to Vercel, API, sync worker, and print worker. Do not mutate orders, shipments, labels, billing, inventory, marketplace state, or shipped/cancelled history during rollback.

liveVerification.reason: The exact implementation SHA was observed Ready/live on Vercel and all three Render services. Read-only environment inspection confirmed durable admission everywhere, role-specific startup logs were healthy, and /health/ready returned HTTP 200. /health/deep transparently remained HTTP 503 only because one existing order-status catch-up pass was partial/backlogged while shipment sync was current and active; all other reported components were green.

caveats.description: npm run test:master:quick was 19 of 20 green because test:daily-orders-trend-count expects a non-null revenue type that already differs at the exact base SHA. PS-447 does not touch the dashboard route, its guard, or the dashboard frontend, so the pre-existing guard drift is excluded from this ticket's closure.
